ingredients: 450 g button or cup mushrooms (2 punnets), whole
60–125 ml thickened or pure cream (1/4–1/2 cup)
method: Rinse the mushrooms and dry them well with a clean tea towel.
Mince the garlic and dice the onion.
Melt the butter in a heavy-based frying pan over medium heat without letting it burn.
Add the garlic and onion and cook for about 1 minute, stirring so nothing burns.
Turn the heat up, add the mushrooms and season with salt.
Stir often for 2–3 minutes, lowering the heat if needed.
Pour in the cream and milk, add the cayenne or paprika, and simmer about 2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Take off the heat once the sauce is as thick as you like.
Sprinkle with parsley and chilli flakes and serve straight away.
name: Creamy garlic mushrooms
tips: No-cream version: skip the cream and milk. Once the mushrooms are golden, add a splash of soy sauce or tamari and fresh thyme, and finish with lemon juice.
Use 1/4 onion and 5 garlic cloves to drop to about 6 g net carbs a serve.
Make it a main by serving it on a steak or with sliced chicken thigh.
verdict: Keto friendly as a side. Most of the carbs come from the garlic and onion, not the mushrooms. Low in protein, so pair it with steak, chicken or eggs. Don't serve it over rice or pasta like the original suggests, as that would spike your blood sugar.
warnings: Low in protein on its own. Serve with steak, chicken or eggs.

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, skin on, boneless
method: The day before (or at least 2 hours ahead), score the skin, pat it very dry and leave uncovered in the fridge.
Rub the meat side (not the skin) with five spice and 1 tbsp tamari. Rub salt into the skin.
Roast at 160°C fan for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Turn up to 230°C and roast 20–30 minutes until the skin crackles all over. Rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir-fry the garlic in sesame oil, add the bok choy and the rest of the tamari, and cook 2–3 minutes.
Slice the pork and serve with the bok choy.
name: Crispy pork belly with garlic bok choy
tips: Leftover slices are great in the kimchi stew.
verdict: Pork belly is close to zero carbs. Have it with greens or cauliflower rice, not white rice. Use tamari or soy sauce, and skip sweet sauces like hoisin or char siu.
warnings: High in calories (about 600 a serve) and saturated fat. Stick to one serve.

ingredients: 2 salmon fillets, skin on (about 180 g each)
method: Pat the salmon skin very dry and season with salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon skin side down for 5–6 minutes, pressing gently, until the skin is crisp.
Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more. Set aside.
Steam or blanch the broccolini for 2–3 minutes.
In the same pan, melt the butter with the garlic until it foams. Add the lemon juice.
Plate the salmon and broccolini and spoon the lemon butter over.
name: Crispy skin salmon with lemon butter and broccolini
tips: Swap in ocean trout or barramundi when they're on special.
verdict: High in protein and healthy fats, low in carbs. A good regular fish night that's easier to sustain than sashimi.

ingredients: 400 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined (frozen is fine)
1 long red chilli, sliced (or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes)
method: Pat the prawns dry and season with salt.
Melt half the butter in a large pan over high heat. Cook the prawns 1–2 minutes a side until just pink, then set aside.
Lower the heat, add the rest of the butter, the garlic and chilli and cook 1 minute.
Add the zucchini noodles and toss 2 minutes until just soft.
Return the prawns, add the lemon juice and parsley and toss. Serve.
name: Garlic butter prawns with zucchini noodles
tips: Add a few sliced mushrooms with the garlic for extra bulk.
Don't overcook the zucchini or it goes watery.
verdict: Prawns are zero carb and cheaper than sashimi. The zucchini noodles stand in for pasta. Frozen Australian prawns work well and keep costs down.

ingredients: 1 thick beef or pork sausage, 90%+ meat, gluten free (about 70 g)
method: Fry the sausage over medium heat for about 12 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Add the bacon and the tomato (cut side down) to the same pan and cook 3–4 minutes.
Push everything to one side, add the butter and the mushrooms and cook until golden.
Wilt the spinach in the pan for 30 seconds.
Fry the eggs in the leftover fat to your liking. Season and serve.
name: Keto full English breakfast
tips: Swap the tomato for extra mushrooms to save about 1.5 g carbs.
Add black pudding only if it's a low-filler one. Most use oats and are high in carbs.
verdict: Everything you love about a fry-up, minus the toast, baked beans and hash brown, which are the parts that spike blood sugar. Check the sausage label: cheap sausages use breadcrumbs or rusk.
warnings: Bacon and sausages are processed and salty. Best as a weekend treat, not daily.

ingredients: 300 g well-fermented kimchi (no added sugar), chopped, plus 3 tbsp of its juice
1 tsp gochujang (optional, no more than this)
300 g firm tofu, cut into cubes
method: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Fry the pork belly 3–4 minutes until it starts to brown.
Add the kimchi, onion and garlic and fry 5 minutes.
Stir in the gochugaru, gochujang (if using), tamari and kimchi juice.
Pour in the water or stock, bring to the boil, then simmer 15–20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer 5 more minutes.
Top with spring onion and serve hot, without rice.
name: Kimchi stew with pork belly (kimchi jjigae)
tips: Crack an egg into each bowl in the last 3 minutes for extra protein.
Older, sourer kimchi has less sugar and more flavour.
verdict: Keto friendly if you leave out the rice and use chilli flakes instead of most of the gochujang, which is high in sugar. Check the kimchi label for added sugar.
warnings: High in salt from the kimchi and soy. Use salt-reduced stock.

ingredients: 1 tin sardines or mackerel in olive oil (about 110 g), drained
Pinch of chilli flakes, salt and pepper
method: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Smash the avocado with lemon, salt and pepper.
Plate the rocket, cucumber, avocado, halved eggs and sardines.
Finish with chilli flakes and a drizzle of oil from the tin.
name: Sardine, egg and avocado plate
tips: Try smoked mussels or salmon in springwater for variety.
Check flavoured tins (tomato sauce, sweet chilli) for added sugar.
verdict: A cheap, no-cook lunch. Tinned sardines or mackerel give you the omega-3s of sashimi for a few dollars a tin.

ingredients: 200 g scotch fillet, at room temperature
Chimichurri: 1/2 cup flat-leaf parsley, 1 garlic clove, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, pinch of chilli flakes, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 20 ml extra virgin olive oil, salt
method: Finely chop the parsley and garlic and mix with the oregano, chilli, vinegar, oil and salt. Let it sit while you cook.
Pat the steak dry and season with salt.
Sear in a very hot pan 2–3 minutes a side for medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry the eggs in butter in the same pan.
Slice the steak, top with chimichurri and serve with the eggs and rocket.
name: Steak and eggs with chimichurri
tips: Make a jar of chimichurri on Sunday. It keeps 5 days in the fridge.
verdict: Almost no carbs and very filling. A big plate, so it can easily be your main meal of the day.
warnings: High in calories (about 735 a plate). Make it the main meal of the day.

ingredients: 300 g beef eye fillet, very cold
1 Lebanese cucumber, thickly sliced, to serve
method: Trim any sinew from the beef and dice it finely by hand (don't mince it).
Mix the eschalot, capers, cornichons, mustard, Worcestershire, Tabasco, oil and parsley in a bowl.
Fold the beef through and season well.
Shape into two rounds on plates, make a small well on top and drop in an egg yolk.
Serve straight away with cucumber slices.
name: Steak tartare with cucumber crisps
tips: Add a few drops of fish sauce or a little anchovy for extra depth with no carbs.
verdict: Very low carb and high protein. Serve on cucumber slices or lettuce cups instead of toast or chips. Use very fresh, good-quality beef from a butcher you trust.
warnings: Raw beef and raw egg yolk. Buy very fresh beef from a butcher and make it the day you buy it.

name: Chanko nabe with chicken meatballs and mushrooms
verdict: A light, brothy sumo hotpot that's high in protein and easy on blood sugar. Skip the udon or rice usually added at the end. Freezes well without the tofu.
ingredients: Meatballs: 500 g chicken thigh mince, 1 egg, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 1 spring onion finely chopped, 1 tbsp tamari or soy sauce, pinch of salt
2 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
method: Mix the meatball ingredients well with your hands. Chill 10 minutes if it's soft.
Bring the stock, tamari and sake to a simmer in a wide pot.
Roll heaped tablespoons of mince into balls and drop them into the broth. Simmer 8 minutes.
Add the wombok stems and shiitake and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the tofu, wombok leaves, bok choy, enoki and spring onion and simmer 3 to 4 minutes more.
Serve at the table straight from the pot.
tips: Make a double batch of meatballs and freeze half raw for next time.
Add sliced pork belly or prawns for a bigger pot.
warnings: Can be salty. Use salt-reduced stock and taste before adding more soy.

name: Pork and kimchi hotpot with mushrooms
verdict: A spicy army-stew style hotpot without the ramen noodles, baked beans or processed meats that push the carbs up. Keep the gochujang to 1 teaspoon.
ingredients: 300 g well-fermented kimchi (no added sugar), chopped
200 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake, oyster or king brown), sliced
method: Mix the gochugaru, gochujang, garlic and tamari into a paste.
Arrange the pork, kimchi, cabbage, mushrooms and tofu in sections in a wide shallow pot. Put the paste in the middle.
Pour in the stock and bring to the boil, then simmer 10 to 12 minutes until the pork is cooked.
Crack the eggs into the broth, add the enoki and simmer 3 minutes.
Top with spring onion and serve at the table.
tips: Swap the pork for leftover crispy pork belly from the recipe on this page.
Add a handful of spinach at the end for more greens.
warnings: High in salt from the kimchi and soy.
Fairly high in calories (about 565 a serve).

name: Shabu shabu hotpot
verdict: Fun to eat at the table and very low carb. Bottled ponzu and sesame dipping sauces often have added sugar, so make the simple dipping sauce below instead.
ingredients: 600 g shabu shabu beef (very thinly sliced scotch fillet, from an Asian grocer)
Dipping sauce: 4 tbsp tamari or soy sauce, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp grated ginger, sliced spring onion
method: Soak the kombu in the water for 30 minutes, then bring it slowly to a simmer and remove the kombu just before it boils.
Mix the dipping sauce and divide into small bowls.
Arrange the beef and vegetables on platters.
Keep the broth simmering at the table (a portable burner works best). Add vegetables, tofu and mushrooms first.
Each person swishes a slice of beef in the broth for 10 to 20 seconds until just cooked, then dips it in the sauce.
Drink the rich broth at the end as soup.
tips: Use thinly sliced pork belly instead of beef for a change.
Leftover broth makes a great base for the egg drop soup.

name: Pork and mushroom miso soup
verdict: A hearty Japanese pork miso soup (tonjiru) without the potato and carrot. Miso has some carbs, so stick to about 3 tablespoons for the pot. Freezes well; add the miso when you reheat if you can.
ingredients: 3 tbsp white or red miso paste
200 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake and shimeji or oyster), sliced
100 g daikon (white radish), cut into thin half-moons
Shichimi or chilli flakes, to serve
method: Heat the sesame oil in a pot and fry the pork 3 minutes until it starts to brown.
Add the mushrooms and daikon and fry 2 minutes.
Pour in the dashi, bring to the boil, skim off any foam and simmer 10 minutes until the daikon is tender.
Add the tofu and cabbage and simmer 3 minutes.
Turn the heat to low. Mix the miso with a ladle of broth until smooth, then stir it in. Don't let it boil after this.
Serve topped with spring onion and shichimi.
tips: Use pork shoulder instead of belly for a leaner soup with more protein.
warnings: High in salt from the miso and dashi. Use salt-reduced dashi or stock.

name: Mushroom egg drop soup
verdict: Ready in 5 to 10 minutes and very low carb. It's light, so add shredded chicken or prawns to make it a meal. Restaurant versions are thickened with cornflour; this one isn't.
method: Bring the stock, ginger, tamari and mushrooms to a simmer and cook 3 minutes.
Stir the soup in a circle, then slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream so they form ribbons.
Leave it for 30 seconds, then stir gently.
Add the sesame oil, white pepper and spring onion and serve.
tips: Add 150 g shredded cooked chicken to bring the protein up to about 30 g a serve.
Leftover shabu shabu broth makes it even better.
warnings: Low in protein and calories on its own. Add chicken or prawns to make it a meal.
